C1_two_subject.easy: Psychologist Asifa Majid and linguist Niclas Burenhult asked speakers of Jahai, a hunter-gatherer language of the Malay Peninsula, to name a series of odors. The Jahai speakers responded concisely and consistently, using abstract smell terms. ______ English speakers given the same odors offered long, varied descriptions, typically naming a likely source of the smell.
C2_belief_finding.easy: Until 2013, rings had been observed only around the solar system’s four giant planets. Few astronomers expected to find them around anything much smaller. ______ that year, a team led by Brazilian astronomer Felipe Braga-Ribas detected two narrow rings encircling Chariklo, an icy body only about 250 kilometers across that orbits the Sun between Saturn and Uranus.
C3_limiting_fact.easy: In the 1930s and early 1940s, Chinese American cinematographer James Wong Howe was one of the most sought-after camera artists in Hollywood, admired for his moody lighting and early use of deep focus. ______ after he was named in testimony as a Communist sympathizer, Howe was graylisted and struggled to find work until director Samuel Fuller hired him in 1950.
E1_consequence.easy: In 2006, bicycles were almost never used for everyday travel in Seville, Spain. Between 2006 and 2010, the city built a connected network of bike lanes physically separated from car traffic. ______ bicycle use in Seville rose about sixfold by 2011, according to researchers at the University of Seville who tracked the number of cyclists at points across the city.
E2_motive_action.easy: Scientists studying Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier wanted measurements from its grounding zone, where the glacier lifts off the seafloor and begins to float. That zone, however, lies beneath roughly 600 meters of ice. ______ in early 2020, a team that included Cornell University scientist Britney Schmidt lowered Icefin, a slender robotic submersible, through a hole drilled down to the ocean below.
P1_purpose_aptness.easy: In architect Takaharu Tezuka’s view, ordinary classrooms, with their walls and fixed routines, go against the way young children naturally learn and play. ______ when he designed Fuji Kindergarten near Tokyo, he used stackable wooden boxes instead of walls to divide the classrooms and turned the building’s oval roof into a playground where children can run in circles.
A1_addition.easy: Pura Belpré, hired in 1921 as the first Puerto Rican employee of the New York Public Library, wanted the library to serve Harlem’s growing Spanish-speaking community. She started bilingual story hours, often acting out Puerto Rican folktales with puppets. ______ she bought Spanish-language books for the library and organized celebrations of Three Kings Day.
X1_example.easy: Many artists working in West Africa today transform discarded consumer goods into monumental works that comment on waste and scarcity. ______ Ghanaian artist Serge Attukwei Clottey cuts up yellow plastic jerrycans, which first came to Ghana holding cooking oil and were later used to store water during shortages, and stitches the pieces together with copper wire into huge wall hangings.
S1_spec_restate.easy: Native American jewelry, pottery, and baskets are frequently copied by non-Native makers. The Indian Arts and Crafts Act of 1990, a truth-in-advertising law, governs how such products are marketed in the United States. ______ the act makes it illegal to offer or sell any art or craft product in a way that falsely suggests it was made by a member of a federally or state-recognized tribe.
M1_emphasis.easy: The Epic of Manas, about a legendary Kyrgyz hero, is traditionally recited from memory by performers called manaschis. Sayakbay Karalaev stood out among them for the sheer size of his repertoire. ______ the version written down from his performances contains more than 500,000 lines, about twenty times the length of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey combined.
T1_sequence_time.easy: Seed collections arriving at the Millennium Seed Bank in southern England spend between two weeks and six months in a drying room kept at 15 percent relative humidity. ______ technicians clean the seeds and X-ray them, discarding any that are empty or damaged by insects. Only then are the seeds dried again and transferred to underground vaults kept at −20°C.
C1_two_subject.medium: In experiments conducted on Barbados, biologist Jean-Nicolas Audet found that bullfinches captured in heavily urbanized parts of the island excelled at innovative foraging tasks, such as opening a drawer to obtain food, and also mounted vigorous immune responses. Bullfinches from rural habitats, ______ solved such problems less readily and exhibited comparatively weak immunity.
C2_belief_finding.medium: Most animals depend on a beating heart to circulate oxygenated fluid through their tissues. The hearts of sea spiders, ______ are so feeble that they propel fluid only within the central body; in a 2017 study of twelve species, biologist H. Arthur Woods and colleagues determined that oxygen reaches the animals’ spindly legs chiefly through peristaltic contractions of gut branches extending into each leg.
E1_consequence.medium: Because red blood cells absorb green light, circulating blood can betray an otherwise translucent frog resting on a leaf. In a 2022 study, biologists Carlos Taboada and Jesse Delia found that sleeping glassfrogs remove nearly 90 percent of their red blood cells from circulation and sequester them in the liver. ______ the resting frogs become two to three times more transparent.
E2_motive_action.medium: After high water on the Rhine and Meuse forced the evacuation of some 250,000 people in 1995, Dutch authorities concluded that continually raising dikes was a losing strategy and that the rivers needed more space to discharge floodwater. ______ the Room for the River program, carried out between 2007 and 2015, moved dikes farther back, excavated high-water channels, and lowered floodplains at 34 locations.
